subject: Escrow vs license amortization: clarifying residency fee split for HIPAA bundle
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@wellnovo.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - WellNovo <contracts@wellnovo.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on SOW credits / residency fee breakdown

Chloe — thanks for the draft SOW. A couple of quick asks from our side before we loop procurement: 1) The SOW shows a one-time escrow/implementation line item (’Evidence escrow & onboarding’) and a separate monthly residency fee for EU/HIPAA. Can you confirm whether Redwood can amortize that one-time escrow fee into monthly license credits instead of billing it up front? 2) If amortized, how does that interact with the residency surcharge — would we get a monthly residency discount during the amortization period? 3) We need clarity on what the ‘evidence’ deliverable includes (audit log export format, retention guarantees, KMS/HSM attestations). Attaching our internal checklist — happy to jump on a quick call.

Tom
Tom Reyes
Head of Platform | WellNovo Health
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@wellnovo.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on SOW credits / residency fee breakdown

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: we can offer amortization of the one-time escrow/onboarding fee as monthly credits; residency surcharge can be partially offset during amortization but not fully waived (details below). I cc’ed Ben (pricing) and Laura (onboarding/SOW) to confirm mechanics.

High-level proposal:
- Option A (Amortize): Spread the one-time escrow fee over 12 months as a recurring monthly credit against the invoice. During that 12-month window, apply a 50% credit to the residency surcharge line so you see a reduced monthly residency charge.
- Option B (Upfront): Pay the escrow one-time up front and receive a 10% one-time implementation discount on onboarding tasks; residency surcharge billed in full each month.

Deliverables: Evidence = audit log export (JSON/NDJSON), weekly snapshot retention guarantee (90 days default, options to extend), KMS key usage logs, and HSM attestation report delivery per SOW milestone. Laura — can you confirm the exact attestation cadence and attachment names?

Attached: WellNovo_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW with redlines), evidence_mapping.xlsx (mapping to our deliverables).

Happy to do a 30-min call tomorrow to align.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@wellnovo.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on SOW credits / residency fee breakdown

Chloe / Laura / Tom — quick pricing note from finance side. We modeled both options to show the customer impact (assumes $120k one-time escrow/onboarding).

- Option A (12-month amortization): $10k/month credit against Redwood recurring charges for 12 months. Residency surcharge is $4k/month pre-credit; apply 50% credit -> $2k/month residency charge net during amortization. Net impact first 12 months = recurring charges reduced by $12k/month ($10k credit + $2k net residency). After month 12, recurring increases by $10k/month (credit falls away) and residency returns to $4k/month unless a new commitment is negotiated.

- Option B (Upfront): WellNovo pays $120k up front; we offer 10% off implementation services (applied to SOW line items). Residency stays at $4k/month.

Considerations / risk allocation: amortization ties Redwood to delivering evidence milestones each quarter; missing milestones would pause credits. For amortization to work we need a 12-month minimum committed ARR threshold (we recommended $500k annualized). If WellNovo prefers lower commitment, Option B cleaner.

Tom — happy to run a simple pro-forma showing your expected cashflow if you want to share target ARR (I can scrub numbers for public decks).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@wellnovo.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on SOW credits / residency fee breakdown

Tom — looping in implementation specifics. Per SOW:
- Evidence deliverables: weekly audit-log snapshots pushed to S3 with NDJSON schema (field-level spec in evidence_mapping.xlsx), monthly HSM attestation PDF, KMS usage report (per-key rotations and access logs) delivered monthly.
- Milestones tied to credits: credits are released monthly contingent on milestone sign-off: Month 1 = onboarding verify, Month 3 = audit ingestion baseline, Month 6 = HSM attestation delivered, Month 12 = retention SLA operational. Missed milestone -> credit pause and remediation plan.

If you prefer amortization but want a lower ARR threshold, we can shift to an 18-month amortization window with smaller monthly credits and a 6-month partial trial period (credits at 50% for months 1–6, full credits thereafter). That reduces Redwood’s short-term exposure.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Tom/Legal to confirm whether WellNovo needs the escrow to be capitalized (accounting) vs expensed — that drives preferability of amortization.
2) If legal OK, Chloe/Ben to send a one-page amendment showing amortization schedule and milestone gating language.
3) Schedule 30-minute call — Chloe, I’m available 10–11am PT Monday.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
